rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill (it has `name: habeas` front matter), so it is a site. It links to three reference files, and each link says when to read the file:
- `references/ci.md` (in "Testing and coverage artifacts"): "Use the [CI example] when adding these steps to an existing workflow" and when setting up or reviewing project CI.
- `references/distributed-requirements.md` (in "Requirements, examples, and definitions"): read it before drafting an obligation that applies at each of many sites, and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`.
- `references/syntax-details.md` (in "References"): read it if a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment, such as a shipped skill or a stylesheet, or if a requirement lives in a nested chapter.

The skill also names other skills' files, such as the habeas-evidence skill's `references/fixme.md`, as plain code-formatted text, not as links. Those names are not links, so the requirement does not govern them. The site has no gaps.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
